questions.question: Which embedding table has trainable parameters in `LearnedPositionalEmbedding`?
options: The position table of shape `(max_context_length, d_model)`
A scalar shared by every position
No table; positions are always computed from token IDs
questions.explanation: The learned implementation owns an `nn.Embedding(max_context_length, d_model)`, so each position vector is updated by optimization. The sinusoidal variant is parameter-free.

questions.question: How many trainable parameters does the sinusoidal positional table add?
questions.explanation: The sinusoidal table is created as a buffer from deterministic sine and cosine values, so it contributes zero trainable parameters.

questions.question: For even dimension `2i`, what value does the sinusoidal table use at position `pos`?
questions.explanation: The implementation follows the standard pair: even dimensions use `sin(pos / base^(2i/d_model))`, while the following odd dimension uses cosine of the same angle.

questions.question: What happens when a learned positional embedding receives a sequence longer than its configured maximum?
options: It wraps positions modulo the maximum.
It pads the extra positions with zeros.
It silently allocates a larger table.
It raises an error instead of indexing past the table.
questions.explanation: The module validates that the sequence length is between one and max_context_length and raises for an overlong sequence. It does not extrapolate or wrap.

questions.question: What must be true before `EmbeddingComposer` can add token and position outputs?
options: The two modules must use the same `d_model`.
The token vocabulary and context length must be equal.
The input batch must contain exactly one sequence.
questions.explanation: Token embeddings have shape `(B, T, D)` and positional embeddings `(T, D)`, so the composer requires matching D dimensions; the latter then broadcasts over B.

questions.question: What shape does the composed embedding have for token IDs shaped `(B, T)` and model width `D`?
questions.explanation: The token lookup produces `(B, T, D)` and the position table produces `(T, D)`. Addition broadcasts the position dimension over the batch, preserving `(B, T, D)`.
